elements.manual_reason: The blue arc backdrop behind the card expands and drops toward the bottom edge; no candidate box isolates it (b01 is the card-area diff).
elements.label: Blue brand arc backdrop

sfx_review.label: music
sfx_review.note: Broadband onset ~660 ms after the motion settles; reads as a music hit/downbeat, not synced to the scale-up.

pattern.description: A small, slightly perspective-tilted dashboard screenshot on a white field with a blue arc grows quickly to fill most of the frame, flattening as it settles, while the arc expands behind it.
pattern.why_premium: Fast front-loaded scale (most of the motion in the first 3-4 frames, then a long settle) gives a confident 'arrive and hold' feel; the backdrop arc scaling with the card adds depth without a hard cut.

build_hint.gsap: tl.fromTo('.dashboard', {scale: 0.45, rotationX: 8, transformPerspective: 1200}, {scale: 1, rotationX: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: 'expo.out'}).fromTo('.arc', {scale: 0.8, yPercent: -10}, {scale: 1, yPercent: 0, duration: 0.4, ease: 'expo.out'}, '<'); no stagger.
build_hint.remotion: const p = spring({frame, fps, config: {damping: 30, stiffness: 220, mass: 1}}); dashboard style transform: `perspective(1200px) rotateX(${interpolate(p,[0,1],[8,0])}deg) scale(${interpolate(p,[0,1],[0.45,1])})`; arc uses the same p for scale and translateY. Critically damped, no overshoot.

notes: camera.move is none; the scale is the card (and arc) growing inside the frame, so it is mapped to ui_camera_push_in as the visual pattern rather than a camera move. Slight perspective tilt in the first frames is a guess from the filmstrip. Inner dashboard text boxes (b02-b20) scale with the card and are not separate elements.
